# Following up: Orlavene Health

**From:** Ruth Calloway <rcalloway@pemberline.com>  
**To:** Marcus Vance <mvance@orlavenehealth.org>  
**Date:** 2/12/26  
**Subject:** Re: Following up: Orlavene Health  

Marcus,

Thank you for making the time for us yesterday afternoon. It was a pleasure walking through your current dock operations and learning more about the receiving bottlenecks at the West Pavilion medical center.

As promised, I am sending over the technical overview for our Gatehouse Check-In workflow and the automated carrier detention alert configuration. Based on what you shared regarding the 5:00 AM courier congestion at Doors 1 through 4, configuring separate appointment pools for cold-chain pharmacy deliveries versus general linen and dietary stock should immediately clear the staging lane on 14th Street. 

I also asked our solutions engineering team to mock up a sample view of the Daily Dock Utilization report tailored to Orlavene's shift handoff schedule at 6:30 AM and 2:30 PM. You will find that PDF attached alongside our standard security whitepaper.

If your team is available next Thursday, 2/19/26, I would welcome the opportunity to run a thirty-minute live sandbox session for your receiving leads so they can see how a yard marshal reassigns a late refrigerated straight truck in Pemberline Dock. Please let me know what window works best on your calendar.

Best regards,

**Ruth Calloway**  
Chief Revenue Officer  
Pemberline Systems  

> **From:** Marcus Vance <mvance@orlavenehealth.org>  
> **To:** Ruth Calloway <rcalloway@pemberline.com>  
> **Date:** 2/11/26  
> **Subject:** Following up: Orlavene Health  
> 
> Hi Ruth,
> 
> Good meeting with you today. If you can send over the documentation on the carrier check-in alerts and the shift handoff reports we discussed for the West Pavilion receiving bays, I will circulate them with my hospital logistics managers ahead of our internal planning review on 2/17/26.
> 
> Thanks,  
> **Marcus Vance**  
> Director of Supply Chain  
> Orlavene Health
